researcher_notes:
MATCH CHECK (re-verified this pass): distinct from P6034 (Hurghada–Safaga, 38.5 km, Hurghada→Safaga, operating). This candidate is Ras Shukeir→Hurghada (127 km) — the upstream Red Sea west-coast trunk that FEEDS Hurghada, whereas P6034 continues Hurghada→Safaga downstream. No existing GEM Egypt gas row covers the Ras Shukeir→Hurghada leg (checked all 57 existing rows incl. names/segments/other-names). Not P6034's parent-under-another-name. => new_row.

ADD-THRESHOLD (all three met): (a) sponsor = GASCO / Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co; (b) endpoints = Egypt, Ras Shukeir (Gulf of Suez) → Hurghada (Red Sea Governorate); (c) concrete step = completed & operating since 2006.

CONFIDENCE = high (upgraded from a prior medium-tier pass). Specs (127 km, 24 in, 7 MMcf/d, EGP 336 million, 2006) are stated by Oil & Gas Journal (Sept 2007), attributing the work to Gasco — verified via url_verifier (200 + 'Shukeir' present), confirmed verbatim: 'Also during 2006, Gasco completed the Shukeir-Hurgada pipeline, 127 km (79 miles) of 24 in. that can handle 7 MMcfd of gas for the Red Sea Governorate ... Estimated cost of the line was L.E. 336 million.' This is independently corroborated on two more fronts: (1) sources/gulfpub (registered Tier-2 reference dataset, PE World Map gas layer, OBJECTID_1 3791) carries its own separately-compiled record named 'Ras Shukheir - Hurghada,' Length=79.0 (miles — matches OGJ's 127 km/79 mi exactly once unit-corrected; the manifest's general 'gas Length = km' convention is a quirk that doesn't hold for this specific record, confirmed by cross-checking the sibling 'Hurghada - Port Safaga Pipeline' record in the same file, whose Length=40.0 IS in km and matches P6034's 38.5 km), Diameter=24, operator 'Egyptian Natural Gas Company [Gasco] (100%)', status Operating, commissioning 'Comm_1'=2007 — a structurally independent database entry (different org, different schema, own contact/GIS provenance) agreeing on name/length/diameter/operator/status with OGJ; (2) GASCO's own official site (Wayback 2020-07-30 capture of gasco.com.eg pipelines page, url_verifier OK + 'Hurghada' present) independently confirms the existence/operator/general routing: '...covering the west coast of the Red Sea reaching Hurghada city' (doesn't name Ras Shukeir specifically or restate the numeric specs, so it corroborates existence/operator/endpoint rather than the exact figures). Two structurally independent sources (OGJ + GulfPub) agree on the precise specs, satisfying the 2+ independent-source bar for high/green; the GASCO primary source is a third, general-existence corroboration. GulfPub's own gas layer also carries a small 'Zeit Bay - Ras Shukheir Line' tie-in (2 km, 16 in) explicitly described as feeding into 'the Ras Shukheir - Hurghada Pipeline' — further reinforcing this is a real, named trunk in an independently-maintained industry database, not an artifact of one journalist's reporting. (Not staged as a separate candidate — out of scope for this vetting pass.)

OWNER: set to 'Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co [100.%]' to match the exact convention on sibling row P6034 and other GASCO-operated Egyptian lines (GASCO is the EGAS transmission subsidiary named in OGJ/GulfPub as builder/operator). No 'Owner [ref]' column exists in this tracker CSV; per project convention owner/operator refs are staged on the separate operators/owners tab, so Owner is intentionally left without an inline [ref]. Flag for the applying researcher: sourced text names GASCO directly as builder/operator, while GEM's tracker convention records the EGAS holding company as Owner — same recurring GASCO-operator/EGAS-owner nuance already logged for other Egypt gas rows (see docs/country_notes/egypt.md), applied here by analogy rather than a value stated for this specific pipeline.

COST: OGJ states 'L.E. 336 million' (Egyptian pounds, 2006); staged as ProjectLevelCost=336000000, ProjectLevelCostUnits='EGP' (tracker convention: units cell holds the bare currency code, the magnitude lives in the number; not converted to USD to avoid introducing an unsourced FX-rate assumption).

ROUTE: endpoints known, no official GIS geometry located (searched EN + AR). RouteAccuracy left at 'no route' / RouteType 'Not mapped (but could be...)' — GulfPub's own corridor sketch (MultiLineString, 2 segments) exists in the registered dataset but is a Tier-2 scrape, not official GIS, so per standing rule it is flagged as a routes-repo PR candidate rather than adopted as this row's RouteAccuracy. Arabic searches surfaced the Ras Shukeir–Hurghada gas plant/port system (MISR Engineering) and an unrelated Ras Bakr–Ras Shukeir CRUDE pipeline (64 km, 18 in — a different commodity/route, not this candidate) but no additional independent gas-pipeline specs.

SOURCE INDEPENDENCE: OGJ, GulfPub, and GASCO's own site are three structurally distinct chains (trade journalism, a commercial industry GIS database, and the operator's own disclosure); OGJ+GulfPub alone already clear the 2-independent-source bar for the numeric specs, so tier=high is warranted (previously logged as medium before the GulfPub cross-check was run this pass).
